chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to us saying: Safwan narrated to us from Isḥāq ibn Ghālib, from his father, from Abū Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Kindness [to parents] and charity given secretly are two things that dispel poverty, increase lifespan, and protect one from seventy bad deaths.

key_terms.الْبَرُّ: Kindness, specifically to parents or maintaining kinship ties

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and physical benefits of giving charity secretly and maintaining family ties?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) highlights that maintaining kinship ties (barr) and giving charity secretly (sadaqat al-sari) serve as spiritual safeguards, removing poverty, extending lifespan, and protecting against seventy types of premature death. This narration, found in *Kitab al-Zuhd*, underscores the practical metaphysical benefits of these acts within Shia tradition, linking social cohesion and hidden piety to divine preservation from calamity.
